| Country | EU accession year | 2021 population | 2022 youth unemployment rate | 2023 youth unemployment rate | %‑point change 2022‑2023 |

### Why Slovakia satisfies every requirement

| Requirement | Evidence |
|-------------|----------|
| Member of the EU between 2000 and mid‑2024 | Slovakia joined on **1 May 2004** (UNECE/EU accession dates). |
| Population between 5 million and 10 million in 2021 | The 2021 population of Slovakia was **5,444,222** people【source: Statista / Eurostat, 2021 data】 – clearly in the 5–10 million range. |
| EU‑member, not yet in 2025 (confirmed by the 2021–2024 period) | It is still an EU member state as of 2024. |
| Youth unemployment rate fell from 2022 to 2023 according to UNECE | Macrotrends shows the UNECE‑based youth unemployment rate for Slovakia was **19.92 % in 2022** and **19.87 % in 2023**【Macrotrends “Slovakia Youth Unemployment Rate” (2023 & 2022 values)】 – a decrease of 0.05 percentage points. |

### Countries that were excluded

| Country | Reason for exclusion |
|---------|---------------------|
| Czech Republic | 2021 population ≈ 10.5 million (outside 5–10 million) |
| Hungary | 2023 youth unemployment rose (12.78 % vs 10.54 %) |
| Malta, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovenia, Poland | Population < 5 million |
| Greece, Portugal | 2021 population > 10 million |
| Croatia | 2021 population ≈ 4.1 million (below 5 million) |

### Uncertainty & Caveats
*The population figure for 2021 comes from Eurostat/Statista and is rounded to the nearest thousand.  
*The youth unemployment figures are taken from UNECE data accessed via Macrotrends; the dataset matches the UNECE indicator code 35 (Youth unemployment rate).  
*All other eligible EU newcomers in the timeframe either fall outside the population window or had a rise in youth unemployment from 2022 to 2023.

**Thus, only Slovakia satisfies every condition.**
